patch_description: The current ansatz uses 24 distinct parameters (8 RY + 8 RZ_pre + 8 RZ_post), each independent per qubit. Since parameter economy strongly dominates the score (fewer distinct trainable parameters is always better, with no diminishing returns), I aggressively reduce parameter count via deliberate sharing: group qubits into two halves (0-3 and 4-7) and share a single rotation parameter within each half for the RY, RZ_pre, and RZ_post layers (2 params each instead of 8, total 6 instead of 24). To compensate for the reduced expressivity and to specifically target the worst-group margin (currently the weak point at 0.35), I add a ring of parameterized CRZ two-qubit gates between the two RZ layers, all sharing a single parameter. This CRZ ring introduces additional nonlinear, correlated entangling structure that can help separate harder-to-classify groups without any extra distinct parameters beyond one new shared name. This should raise parameter efficiency substantially while preserving or improving separation quality via the new entangling structure.
